title: Applied Ethics: Medical, Environmental, Sexual
welcome_lead: Apply religious ethical frameworks to medicine, the environment and sexual life.
meta_desc: Religious Studies Adventure: applied religious ethics in medical, environmental and sexual contexts.
final_note: You have brought ethical traditions into contact with hard cases. Religious ethics is living dialogue.

walkthroughs.body_html: Religious traditions debate abortion, end-of-life care and reproductive technologies. Catholic natural law opposes most direct termination of life; Jewish bioethics often weighs the principle of pikuach nefesh (saving life); Buddhist ethics emphasises intention and reduction of suffering; Islamic ethics references maqasid al-shari'a (objectives of the law).

Stewardship traditions (Genesis 2:15) frame human responsibility. Pope Francis's Laudato Si' (2015) develops 'integral ecology' linking environmental and social justice. Hindu and Buddhist ahimsa grounds vegetarian and ecological practice; Islamic khalifa implies trusteeship of creation.

Religious traditions vary widely on sexual ethics. Catholic and Orthodox traditions emphasise procreation within marriage; many Protestant, Jewish and Buddhist communities have embraced revised understandings, including same-sex relationships and gender identity, while others uphold traditional teachings. Dialogue is ongoing in pluralistic societies.

mcqs.q: What was the Augustine vs Pelagius dispute about original sin?
options: Pelagius and Augustine agreed humans are born innocent.
Karma is a god who decides what happens to you.

Augustine argued humans inherit a corrupted nature from Adam (original sin) and cannot achieve salvation without grace; Pelagius argued humans retain free will to choose good without divine intervention and that sin is imitated, not inherited.
Original sin means Christians believe babies are evil.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between Sunni and Shia Islam?
options: Sunnis follow the Quran and Shias follow the Bible.
Sunnis and Shias believe in different gods.
Pelagius and Augustine agreed humans are born innocent.
They split over who should lead the Muslim community after Muhammad: Sunnis accepted Abu Bakr and elected caliphs; Shias believed leadership should follow Muhammad's bloodline through Ali.

mcqs.q: What does karma mean in Hindu and Buddhist thought?
options: Sunnis follow the Quran and Shias follow the Bible.
The principle that actions have moral consequences shaping future experience or rebirth — not fate, but ethical cause and effect built into reality.
Karma is when bad things happen to bad people as punishment.
Karma is a god who decides what happens to you.
